messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager SEV2  Ingress / API gateway showing sudden 502/504 surge in us-west-2. 5xx rate 22% over 3m, spike in gateway 502 and upstream timeouts. Auto-snapshot: https://metrics.redwood.example/ingress/us-west-2?span=3m

rachel (ingress-oncall): I'm oncall  pulling dashboards and logs. Beginning triage. Error spike aligns with 02:12Z. Not seeing config deploys at that exact time.

deploy-bot: Recent deploys: canary ingress-edge-config v2.12 promoted at 02:05Z to 10% of traffic (job 9921). Full rollout not started.

tom (edge): I see a pattern of upstream connection resets hitting svc-auth and svc-embed. Edge TLS frontends show many keepalive timeouts and worker saturation. Could be sudden burst of long-lived upstreams causing accept queue backlog.

nina (platform): also seeing increased ephemeral port exhaustion on a subset of nodes (10.4.2.11, 10.4.2.13). I'm of the opinion we should remove the bad nodes from LB and scale ingress proxies up while we investigate.

rachel (ingress-oncall): Agreed. Plan: 1) scale ingress-edge replicas in us-west-2 4 -> 10 2) drain and remove 10.4.2.11 from pool 3) bump backend idle timeout to reduce stuck sockets temporarily. Executing now.

rachel (ingress-oncall): Scaling command: ```bash
kubectl -n infra scale deploy/ingress-edge --replicas=10 -l region=us-west-2
```deploy-bot: Scale job started (job/10134). Watch: https://deploys.redwood.example/jobs/10134

rachel (ingress-oncall): Draining host 10.4.2.11 from LB: ```
curl -X POST https://internal-lb.redwood.example/pools/us-west-2/remove -d '{"host":"10.4.2.11"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***'
```ops-bot: Host 10.4.2.11 removed from pool, marked UNHEALTHY. Connection drain initiated.

cs-bot: customer-impact: 9 tenants showing >10% error rates in last 10m, 1 tenant >60%. CS notified and incident status page updated. https://status.redwood.example/incidents/INC-2026-342

tom (edge): Also toggling ingress keepalive settings: reducing keepalive_requests and enabling fast_close on the edge to free sockets faster. Applying change to canary config subset first.

rachel (ingress-oncall): Observed logs (excerpt): ```
[2026-03-15T02:13:22Z] ingress-edge[pod-12] WARN upstream timeout proxying to 10.4.2.11:443 (svc-auth)
[2026-03-15T02:13:22Z] ingress-edge[pod-08] ERROR accept queue full, new connections rejected
```

nina (platform): While scaling finishes, I'll prepare a traffic diversion plan to us-east-1 for up to 25% of traffic if errors don't drop. Ready to execute on a thumbs-up.

rachel (ingress-oncall): replicas now scaling, 6 new pods coming up. Monitoring realtime. Error rate fell from 22% -> 9% in 90s.

deploy-bot: Scale job 10134 completed successfully. New pod list: ingress-edge-pod-{20..25}.

rachel (ingress-oncall): Rolling restart of the affected backend nodes' sidecars (svc-auth sidecar) to clear CLOSE_WAIT sockets: ```bash
kubectl -n services rollout restart ds/auth-sidecar -l node=10.4.2.11
```ops-bot: Sidecar restart triggered.

rachel (ingress-oncall): Error rate now 4.1% and trending down. Latency back to baseline for 95th. No need to shift traffic yet.

tom (edge): Recommend follow-ups: 1) kernel tcp_tw_reuse and ephemeral port tuning on nodes 2) tune ingress worker_rlimit_nofile 3) circuit breaker on svc-auth with fast-fail to reduce head-of-line blocking.

nina (platform): I'll create an incident task list and schedule postmortem. Also marking the canary ingress-config v2.12 for rollback investigation even though it was only at 10% traffic.

rachel (ingress-oncall): lowering severity to SEV3 at 02:17Z, will continue monitoring for 30m. Handing off to tom for RCA and platform follow-ups.

cs-bot: Customer update sent: summary, mitigation, estimated remediation timeline. Ticket: https://support.redwood.example/tickets/INC-2026-342-1

ops-bot: Incident follow-ups created: INC-2026-342: RCA, kernel tuning, LB automation for unhealthy-host removal, alert for accept-queue/full events. Assigned: tom, nina.

tom (edge): I'll take the RCA. Initial hypothesis: transient socket backlog on backend nodes caused upstream resets -> gateway 502/504 spike. Will validate with packet captures and kernel metrics.

rachel (ingress-oncall): leaving channel  monitoring handed to platform. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Severity changed to SEV3. If 5xx > 8% for 10m re-open SEV2 and notify oncall. Thread archived to incident tracker when follow-ups created.
